facts.fact: Black requires Python 3.10 or newer to run.
facts.source_quote: _Black_ can be installed by running `pip install black`. It requires Python 3.10+ to

facts.fact: Black no longer supports formatting Python 2 code; that support was removed in version 22.0.
facts.source_quote: Support for formatting Python 2 code was removed in version 22.0.

facts.fact: Black supports running on PyPy 3.8 and higher (PyPy 3.7 is no longer supported).
facts.source_quote: Yes, there is support for PyPy 3.8 and higher.

facts.fact: Black is stable (no longer a beta product): formatting output is stable for all releases within the same calendar year.
facts.source_quote: Starting in 2022, the formatting output is stable for the releases made in the same year

facts.fact: The --experimental-string-processing flag has been removed (in 24.1.0); string splitting is now only available as the unstable feature string_processing via --preview --enable-unstable-feature string_processing.

docs.inserted: If you only want the long string splitting, pass the `--experimental-string-processing` flag instead.
Release 21.12b0, published in December 2021, was the last version of _Black_ able to format Python 2 code.
Until version 24.1.0 removed it, long string splitting could also be requested with the deprecated `--experimental-string-processing` flag.
